text: Thank you for sharing your history. To better understand your knee pain, can you describe the specific location of the pain and when it started after increasing your physical activity?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the pain been localized to the front of the knee, specifically around the kneecap, or does it feel more like a deep ache within the joint itself? REQUEST TEST: Knee_MRI. REQUEST IMAGES: Knee_MRI_images.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints)

Your mention of pneumonia seems unrelated to your current knee symptoms; the location you described just below the kneecap on the inner side, combined with your recent volleyball activity, strongly suggests stress on the shin bone or surrounding tissue. Given the pain specifically under the patella and the mechanism of injury, we should also rule out a patellar tendon issue, but the stress syndrome is the most likely culprit based on your activity level.
